17.1.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.1.text: Arjuna said: "What is the state of those who remain faithful but neglect the scriptural injunctions—is it sattva, rajas, or tamas? O Krsna!"

17.1.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.1.text: Arjuna said, "Now, O Krsna, what is the position or basis of those who, despite leaving aside the injunction of the Sastra, still worship with faith? Is it Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas?"

17.1.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.1.text: Arjuna said, But, O Krsna, what is the state of those who, endued with faith, perform sacrifices, distribute wealth, etc. in honour of gods and others, while ignoring the injunctions of the scriptures? Is it sattva, rajas, or tamas?

17.1.author: Swami Sivananda
17.1.text: Arjuna said, "What is the condition of those who, disregarding the injunctions of the scriptures, perform sacrifice with faith—is it Sattva, Rajas, or Tamas, O Krishna?"

17.1.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.1.text: Arjuna asked, "My Lord, what is the condition of those who perform acts of sacrifice not according to the scriptures, but with implicit faith? Is it one of purity, passion, or ignorance?"

17.2.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.2.text: The Bhagavat said, "The faith of the embodied persons is born of their nature and is of three kinds [viz.]: that which is made of Sattva; that which is made of Rajas; and that which is made of Tamas. Listen about them."

17.2.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.2.text: The Lord said, "The faith of embodied beings is threefold, born of their own nature and constituted of Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas. Now, listen to me about it."

17.2.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.2.text: The Blessed Lord said, "That faith of the embodied beings, born of their own nature, is threefold—born of sattva, rajas, and tamas. Hear about it."

17.2.author: Swami Sivananda
17.2.text: The Blessed Lord said, "There are threefold faiths inherent in the nature of the embodied: the sattvic (pure), the rajasic (passionate), and the tamasic (dark). Hear of them."

17.2.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.2.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Man has an inherent faith in one or another of the qualities—purity, passion, and ignorance. Now, listen.

17.3.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.3.text: Corresponding to one's own sattva, O descendant of Bharata, everybody has faith. The person predominantly consists of faith. Whatever one has faith in, that he becomes certainly.

17.3.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.3.text: O Arjuna, the faith of everyone is in accordance with their inner organ (Antahkarana). Each person consists of faith; whatever their faith is, that is who they are.

17.3.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.3.text: O scion of the Bharata dynasty, the faith of all beings is in accordance with their minds. This person is composed of faith as the dominant factor. He is indeed what his faith is.

17.3.author: Swami Sivananda
17.3.text: The faith of each is in accordance with their nature, O Arjuna. People consist of their faith; as a person's faith is, so are they.

17.3.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.3.text: Every person's faith conforms to their nature. By nature, they are full of faith. They are, in fact, what their faith makes them.

17.4.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.4.text: The men of the Sattva strand perform sacrifices intending for the gods; the men of the Rajas strand do so for the spirits and demons; and the men of the Tamas strand perform sacrifices intending for the imps, the dead, and the ghosts.

17.4.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.4.text: The sattvic types worship the gods; the rajasic types worship yaksas and rakshasas; and the others, the tamasic types, worship the departed ancestors and hosts of bhutas.

17.4.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.4.text: Those with sattva quality worship the gods; those with rajas, the demigods and demons; and those with tamas, ghosts and hosts of spirits.

17.4.author: Swami Sivananda
17.4.text: The sattvic, or pure, men worship the gods; the rajasic, or passionate, worship the yakshas and rakshasas; the others, the tamasic or deluded people, worship ghosts and hosts of nature-spirits.

17.4.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.4.text: The pure worship the true God; the passionate, the powers of wealth and magic; the ignorant, the spirits of the dead and lower orders of nature.

17.5.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.5.text: Those men who practise terrible austerities not as enjoined in the scriptures, who are bound by hypocrisy and conceit, and are impelled by the force of passion for desired objects;

17.5.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.5.text: Those men who practice terrible austerities not enjoined by the scriptures, given to ostentation and conceit, and prompted by the force of sensual desires and passions;

17.5.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.5.text: Those persons who, given to ostentation and pride, and possessed of passion, attachment, and strength, undertake severe austerities not sanctioned by the scriptures;

17.5.author: Swami Sivananda
17.5.text: Those men who practice terrific austerities not prescribed by the scriptures, given to hypocrisy and egoism, driven by the force of lust and attachment.

17.5.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.5.text: Those who practice austerities not commanded by scripture, who are enslaved to hypocrisy and egotism, who are carried away by the fury of desire and passion,

17.6.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.6.text: Those who unintelligently emaciate the conglomeration of elements in their physical body and emaciate Me, dwelling within the physical body—know them to be of a demoniac resolve.

17.6.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.6.text: These foolish men, who torture the group of elements in their bodies and Me, who dwell within the body—know them to be demoniacal in their resolves.

17.6.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.6.text: (And those who,) being non-discriminating, torture all the organs in the body as well as even Me who reside in the body—know them to be possessed of demoniacal conviction.

17.6.author: Swami Sivananda
17.6.text: Know thou these to be of demonical resolves, senselessly torturing all the elements in the body and Me who dwell in the body.

17.6.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.6.text: They are ignorant and torment the organs of the body, harassing Me who lives within. Know that they are devoted to evil.

17.7.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.7.text: Further, the food which is dear to all is of three kinds. So too are their sacrifice, austerity, and charity. Listen to this distinction of them.

17.7.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.7.text: Even the food that is dear to all is threefold; so too are sacrifices, austerities, and gifts. Listen to this distinction among them.

17.7.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.7.text: Food, which is dear to all, is of three kinds; likewise, sacrifices, austerity, and charity are also of three kinds. Listen to this classification of them.

17.7.author: Swami Sivananda
17.7.text: The food that is dear to each is threefold, as well as sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Hear the distinction of these.

17.7.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.7.text: The food that people enjoy is also threefold, like the ways of sacrifice, austerity, and almsgiving. Listen to the distinction.

17.8.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.8.text: The foods that increase life, energy, strength, good health, happiness, and satisfaction; which are delicious, soft, substantial, and pleasant to the heart (stomach); they are dear to the men of the Sattva strand.

17.8.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.8.text: Foods that promote longevity, intellectual alertness, strength, health, pleasure, and happiness, and those that are sweet, oily, substantial, and agreeable, are dear to sattvic men.

17.8.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.8.text: Foods that augment life, firmness of mind, strength, health, happiness, and delight, and which are succulent, oleaginous, substantial, and agreeable, are dear to one endowed with sattva.

17.8.author: Swami Sivananda
17.8.text: The foods that increase life, purity, strength, health, joy, and cheerfulness (good appetite), which are savory, oily, substantial, and agreeable, are dear to the Sattvic (pure) people.

17.8.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.8.text: The foods that prolong life, increase purity, vigour, health, cheerfulness, and happiness are those that are delicious, soothing, substantial, and agreeable; these are loved by the pure.

17.9.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.9.text: The foods killed by men of the Rajas strand are those that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, harsh, dry, and burning; and which cause pain, grief, and disease.

17.9.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.9.text: Foods that are bitter, sour, very salty, excessively heating, highly pungent, dry, and burning are all dear to Rajasika men; they cause pain, sorrow, and disease.

17.9.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.9.text: Foods that are bitter, sour, salty, very hot, pungent, dry, and burning, producing pain, sorrow, and disease, are dear to one who has rajas.

17.9.author: Swami Sivananda
17.9.text: The foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning are liked by the Rajasic and are productive of pain, grief, and disease.

17.9.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.9.text: Those in whom passion is dominant like foods that are bitter, sour, salty, overly hot, pungent, dry, and burning. These produce unhappiness, repentance, and disease.

17.10.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.10.text: What is old, tasteless, foul-smelling, and stale; what is also left over after eating, and is impure - such food is dear to the men of Tamas (Strand).

17.10.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.10.text: That food which is stale, tasteless, putrid, decayed, rejected, unclean, is dear to those of a Tamasic nature.

17.10.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.10.text: Food that is not properly cooked, lacking in essence, putrid and stale, as well as that which is unfit for sacrifice, is dear to one possessed of tamas.

17.10.author: Swami Sivananda
17.10.text: That which is stale, tasteless, putrid, rotten, rejected, and impure is the food liked by the Tamasic.

17.10.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.10.text: The ignorant love food that is stale, not nourishing, putrid, and corrupt; the leftovers of others, and unclean.

17.11.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.11.text: That sacrifice of the Sattva (Strand) is offered, as prescribed, by those who desire no reward, steadying their minds with the thought that it is simply something to be offered.

17.11.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.11.text: The sacrifice (worship) marked by Sattva is what is offered by those who desire no fruit and have the conviction that it should be performed as prescribed in the scriptures.

17.11.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.11.text: That sacrifice which is in accordance with the injunctions, performed by persons who do not hanker after results, and with the mental conviction that it is surely obligatory, is done through sattva.

17.11.author: Swami Sivananda
17.11.text: That sacrifice which is offered by men without desire for reward, as enjoined by the ordinance (scripture), with a firm faith that doing so is their duty, is Sattvic or pure.

17.11.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.11.text: Sacrifice is pure when it is offered by one who does not covet the fruit of it, when it is done according to the commands of scripture, and with implicit faith that the sacrifice is a duty.

17.12.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.12.text: What is offered aiming at fruit and also only for the sake of display—know that sacrifice to be of the Rajas strand and to be transitory and impermanent.

17.12.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.12.text: But that sacrifice which is offered with the intention of gaining a reward and for the sake of show, know it, O Arjuna, to be Rajasic.

17.12.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.12.text: But that sacrifice which is performed with an aim for a result, as well as for show—know that sacrifice to be done through rajas, O greatest among the descendants of Bharata.

17.12.author: Swami Sivananda
17.12.text: The sacrifice that is offered, O Arjuna, seeking a reward and for show, know that to be a Rajasic Yajna.

17.12.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.12.text: Sacrifice which is performed for the sake of its results, or for self-glorification - that, O best of Aryans, is the product of passion.

17.13.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.13.text: They declare that sacrifice to be of the Tamas (Strand) which is devoid of scriptural injunction, in which there is no recitation of Vedic hymns, where no food and sacrificial fee are distributed, and which is completely devoid of faith.

17.13.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.13.text: That sacrifice which is devoid of authority, which uses offerings not sanctioned by the Sastras, which is performed without recitation of hymns and devoid of gifts and faith - that, they say, is marked by Tamas.

17.13.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.13.text: They declare that sacrifice as 'done through tamas' which is contrary to injunction, in which no food is distributed, in which no mantras are used, in which no offerings are made to priests, and which is devoid of faith.

17.13.author: Swami Sivananda
17.13.text: They declare that sacrifice to be Tamasic which is contrary to the ordinances of the scriptures, in which no food is distributed, and which is devoid of mantras, gifts, and faith.

17.13.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.13.text: Sacrifice that is contrary to scriptural command, that is unaccompanied by prayers or gifts of food or money, and is without faith—that is the product of ignorance.

17.14.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.14.text: The worship of the gods, the twice-born, the elders, and the wise; purity, honesty, continence, and harmlessness—all this is said to be bodily austerity.

17.14.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.14.text: Worshiping the gods, the twice-born, the preceptors, the enlightened ones, practicing purity, uprightness, continence, and non-injury—these are called austerity of the body.

17.14.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.14.text: The worship of gods, twice-borns, venerable persons, and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, and non-injury—these are said to be bodily austerities.

17.14.author: Swami Sivananda
17.14.text: Worship of the gods, the twice-born, the teachers, and the wise; purity, straightforwardness, celibacy, and non-injury are all called the austerities of the body.

17.14.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.14.text: Worship of God and the Master; respect for the preacher and the philosopher; purity, rectitude, continence, and harmlessness—all of these constitute physical austerity.

17.15.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.15.text: The unoffending speech which is true, pleasant, and beneficial; as well as the practice of regular recitation of the Vedas—all this is said to be an austerity of the speech-sense.

17.15.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.15.text: Speech that causes no shock, is true, pleasant, and beneficial, and also the practice of reciting scriptures, is called the austerity of speech.

17.15.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.15.text: That speech which causes no pain, which is true, agreeable, and beneficial; as well as the practice of studying the scriptures—is said to be the austerity of speech.

17.15.author: Swami Sivananda
17.15.text: Speech that causes no excitement, is truthful, pleasant, and beneficial; the practice of studying the Vedas is called austerity of speech.

17.15.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.15.text: Speech that hurts no one, that is true, pleasant to listen to, and beneficial, and the constant study of the scriptures—this is austerity of speech.

17.16.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.16.text: The serenity of mind, the stillness, the taciturnity, the self-control, the purity of thought—all this is called mental austerity.

17.16.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.16.text: Serenity of mind, benevolence, silence, self-control, and purity of mind—these are known as austerity of the mind.

17.16.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.16.text: Tranquility of mind, gentleness, reticence, withdrawal of the mind, purity of heart—these are what are called mental austerities.

17.16.author: Swami Sivananda
17.16.text: Serenity of mind, good-heartedness, self-control, and purity of nature—this is called mental austerity.

17.16.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.16.text: Serenity, kindness, silence, self-control, and purity—these are the austerities of the mind.

17.17.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.17.text: This three-fold austerity, observed with best faith, by men who are masters of Yoga and have no desire for its fruits—they call it to be of the Sattva.

17.17.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.17.text: The threefold austerity, practiced with supreme faith by men who desire no fruit and are devoted—they call it austerity of Sattva.

17.17.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.17.text: When that threefold austerity is undertaken with supreme faith by people who do not hanker after results and are self-controlled, they speak of it as being born of sattva.

17.17.author: Swami Sivananda
17.17.text: This threefold austerity, practiced by steadfast men, with the utmost faith, desiring no reward, is called Sattvic.

17.17.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.17.text: These threefold austerities, performed with faith and without thought of reward, can truly be considered pure.

17.18.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.18.text: The austerity that is practiced for gaining respect, honor, and reverence, and with sheer show—that is called here [austerity] of the Rajas, and it is unstable and impermanent.

17.18.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.18.text: That austerity, practiced with ostentation for the sake of gaining respect, praise, and reverence, is here said to be Rajasa. It is unsteady and impermanent.

17.18.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.18.text: That austerity which is undertaken for earning a name, being honored and worshipped, and also ostentatiously—that is spoken of as born of rajas, belonging to this world, uncertain, and transitory.

17.18.author: Swami Sivananda
17.18.text: The austerity that is practiced with the aim of gaining good reception, honor, and worship, and with hypocrisy, is said to be Rajasic, unstable, and transient.

17.18.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.18.text: Austerity coupled with hypocrisy, or performed for the sake of self-glorification, popularity, or vanity, comes from passion, and its result is always uncertain and temporary.

17.19.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.19.text: What austerity is practised with foolish obstinacy and self-torture only in order to destroy others—that is declared to be of the Tamas.

17.19.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.19.text: That austerity which is practised from deluded notions by means of self-torture or to injure another is said to be Tamasika.

17.19.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.19.text: That austerity which is undertaken with a foolish intent, causing pain to oneself or for the destruction of others, is said to be born of tamas.

17.19.author: Swami Sivananda
17.19.text: That austerity which is practised out of a foolish notion, with self-torture, or for the purpose of destroying another, is declared to be of the Tamasic nature.

17.19.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.19.text: Austerity done under delusion, and accompanied with sorcery or the infliction of pain upon oneself or another, may be assumed to spring from ignorance.

17.20.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.20.text: A gift that is given with the thought that 'one must give' and is given in an appropriate place and at the right time to a worthy person who is unable to repay—that gift is considered to be of the Sattva.

17.20.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.20.text: Gifts given with the feeling that it is one's own duty to give, to one who makes no return, at the proper place and time to the deserving person—that is said to be sattvika.

17.20.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.20.text: That gift is referred to as born of sattva which is given with the idea that it should be given, to one who will not serve in return, at the right place, right time, and to the right person.

17.20.author: Swami Sivananda
17.20.text: That gift which is given to one who does nothing in return, knowing it to be a duty to give in a suitable place and time to a worthy person, is held to be Sattvic.

17.20.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.20.text: The gift that is given without thought of recompense, believing it should be made, in an appropriate place, at an opportune time, and to a deserving person—such a gift is pure.

17.21.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.21.text: But what is given in return for a favor, or with the expectation of a reward, and which is done with much agitation—that gift is said to be of the Rajas.

17.21.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.21.text: But that which is given as a consideration for something received or in expectation of a future reward, or grudgingly, is called a Rajasika gift.

17.21.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.21.text: But the gift which is given expecting reciprocation, or with a desire for its result, and grudgingly, is considered to be born of rajas.

17.21.author: Swami Sivananda
17.21.text: And, that gift which is given with the intention of receiving something in return, or expecting a reward, or begrudgingly, is considered to be Rajasic.

17.21.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.21.text: That which is given for the sake of the results it will produce, or with the hope of recompense, or grudgingly—that may truly be said to be the outcome of passion.

17.22.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.22.text: The gift which is given at an inappropriate place, time, and to unworthy persons, and which is converted into a bad act and is disrespected—that is declared to be of the Tamas.

17.22.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.22.text: That gift which is given at the wrong place, wrong time, to an unworthy recipient, without due respect and with contempt, is called the gift of a Tamasa nature.

17.22.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.22.text: The gift which is made at an inappropriate place and time, and to undeserving persons, without proper respect and with disdain, is declared to be born of tamas.

17.22.author: Swami Sivananda
17.22.text: The gift that is given in the wrong place and at the wrong time, to unworthy persons, without respect or with insult, is declared to be of a Tamasic nature.

17.22.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.22.text: And that which is given at an inappropriate place or time or to one who is undeserving, or with disrespect or contempt - such a gift is the result of ignorance.

17.23.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.23.text: OM TAT SAT: This is held to be the three-fold indication of Brahman. Through this, the Vedas and sacrifices were fashioned by Brahma in the past.

17.23.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.23.text: Om, Tat, Sat—thus, Brahman is denoted by this threefold expression. In the past, Brahmanas, the Vedas, and sacrifices were ordained in association with these.

17.23.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.23.text: "Om-tat-sat" - this is considered to be the threefold designation of Brahman. The Brahmanas, Vedas, and sacrifices were ordained by that in days of yore.

17.23.author: Swami Sivananda
17.23.text: "Om Tat Sat": This has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman. By that, the Brahmanas, the Vedas, and the sacrifices were created formerly.

17.23.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.23.text: Om Tat Sat is the triple designation of the Eternal Spirit, by which the Vedic Scriptures, ceremonials, and sacrifices were ordained of old.

17.24.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.24.text: Therefore, the scripture-prescribed acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity of those who are habituated to having Brahman-discourses invariably commence with the utterance of OM.

17.24.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.24.text: Therefore, the Veda-enjoined sacrificial acts, gifts, and austerities, expounded by the Vedas, or those belonging to the first three stations, are always begun after pronouncing Om at the beginning.

17.24.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.24.text: Therefore, acts of sacrifice, charity, and austerity, as prescribed through injunctions, of those who study and expound the Vedas, always commence after uttering the syllable ‘Om’.

17.24.author: Swami Sivananda
17.24.text: Therefore, with the utterance of "Om," the acts of sacrifice, gift, and austerity, as enjoined in the scriptures, are always begun by the students of Brahman.

17.24.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.24.text: Therefore, all acts of sacrifice, gifts, and austerities prescribed by the scriptures are always begun by those who understand the Spirit with the word "Om."

17.25.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.25.text: With the utterance of TAT, and without aiming for the fruit, those who seek emancipation perform acts of sacrifice, austerity, and various acts of giving.

17.25.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.25.text: Acts of sacrifice, austerity, and various gifts are performed without aiming at a reward by those who seek release, after pronouncing Tat.

17.25.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.25.text: After uttering the word "tat," acts of sacrifice and austerity, as well as various acts of charity, are performed without regard for results by persons aspiring for liberation.

17.25.author: Swami Sivananda
17.25.text: Uttering "Tat," without aiming for the fruits, are the acts of sacrifice, austerity, and the various acts of gifts performed by those seeking liberation.

17.25.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.25.text: Those who desire deliverance begin their acts of sacrifice, austerity, or gift with the word "Tat" (meaning "That"), without thought of reward.

17.26.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.26.text: In the sense of 'right' (or 'manifesting as being') and in the sense of 'proper' (or 'manifesting perfectly'), this word SAT is employed. Likewise, the word SAT is used with regard to the praiseworthy act; O son of Prtha!

17.26.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.26.text: This term "Sat" is used in the sense of existence and goodness. And so also, O Arjuna, the word "Sat" is applied to an auspicious action.

17.26.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.26.text: This word "sat" is used with regard to something coming into being and someone becoming good. Likewise, O son of Prtha, the word "sat" is used with regard to an auspicious rite.

17.26.author: Swami Sivananda
17.26.text: The word "Sat" is used to refer to reality and goodness; likewise, O Arjuna, the word "Sat" is used to refer to an auspicious act.

17.26.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.26.text: Sat' means Reality or the highest Good, and also, O Arjuna, it is used to denote an action of exceptional merit.

17.27.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.27.text: Steadfastness is performing sacrifice, austerity, and giving gifts; this act is hence justly called SAT.

17.27.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.27.text: Devotion to sacrifice, austerity, and gifts is also referred to as Sat; and thus, any action for such purposes is known as Sat.

17.27.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.27.text: And the steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and charity is spoken of as sat (good). And even the action meant for these is, indeed, called as sat.

17.27.author: Swami Sivananda
17.27.text: Steadfastness in sacrifice, austerity, and gift is also called 'Sat', and action in connection with these, or for the sake of the Supreme, is also called 'Sat'.

17.27.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.27.text: Conviction in sacrifice, austerity, and giving is also called Sat. So too, an action done only for the Lord's sake.

17.28.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
17.28.text: Without faith, whatever oblation is offered, whatever gift is made, whatever austerity is practiced, and whatever action is undertaken, that is called ASAT and it is of no avail after one's death or in this world.

17.28.author: Swami Adidevananda
17.28.text: Whatever offering or gift is made, whatever austerity is practiced, and whatever action is performed without faith, that is called Asat, O Arjuna. It is of no value here or hereafter.

17.28.author: Swami Gambirananda
17.28.text: O son of Prtha, whatever is offered in sacrifice and given in charity, as also whatever austerity is undertaken or whatever is done without faith, is said to be of no avail. And it is of no consequence after death, nor here.

17.28.author: Swami Sivananda
17.28.text: Whatever is sacrificed, given, or performed, and whatever austerity is practiced without faith, it is called 'Asat', O Arjuna; it is of no value here or hereafter (after death).

17.28.author: Shri Purohit Swami
17.28.text: Whatever is done without faith, whether it be sacrifice, austerity, gift, or anything else, is called Asat (meaning "Unreal"), for it is the negation of Sat, O Arjuna! Such an act has no significance, here or hereafter.
